title: Music Trivia Live: Complete Five-Round Question Bank
audience: 10–20 work colleagues; broad, mixed music knowledge

deliveryRules.audioPlayback: Host/shared-screen only. Do not send or autoplay audio on player phones.
deliveryRules.hostInstruction: Share the Chrome tab with tab audio enabled; play each audio item after opening the question.
deliveryRules.clipProduction: Use legally licensed, internally cleared, or permissioned clips. Suggested windows are editorial cues, not supplied audio.
deliveryRules.lyrics: Prompts intentionally contain only short excerpts or blanks; do not expand them into full lines or verses. Obtain lyric-display rights if required.

scoringSummary.rounds1to4: 25 base points (Rounds 1, 3, and 4 are five points each; Round 2 is a 10-point featured round)
scoringSummary.finale: 10 points (one per correctly matched piano intro)
scoringSummary.tieBreak: Use the optional nearest-number tie-break only if needed after the finale.

rounds.title: Round 1 — Name That Tune
rounds.intro: Five short, host-played clips. Trust the first song that pops into your head.
rounds.hostPacing: Open each item, play the clip once, allow one replay on request, then lock after 20–25 seconds.

questions.prompt: Which song features this legendary guitar solo?

audio.cue: Use the opening of Eddie Van Halen’s guitar solo from Beat It.

questions.hostReveal: Beat It — Michael Jackson. The solo is played by Eddie Van Halen.
questions.accessibility: Display ‘Audio clip 1’ only; do not expose filenames or artist metadata before reveal.

questions.prompt: Which song opens with this instantly recognizable banjo-driven hook?

audio.cue: Use the opening banjo/guitar hook from Old Town Road before vocals.

questions.hostReveal: Old Town Road — Lil Nas X.
questions.accessibility: Offer one replay; no player-device playback.

questions.prompt: Type the title of this dance-floor classic.

audio.cue: Use the instrumental build immediately before the first big chorus.

questions.hostReviewGuidance: Accept only the song title; do not require Mark Ronson or Bruno Mars.
questions.hostReveal: Uptown Funk — Mark Ronson featuring Bruno Mars.

audio.cue: Use the opening synth hook from Blinding Lights.

rounds.title: Round 2 — Movie Songs
rounds.intro: Songs that became inseparable from the films that put them on screen.
rounds.hostPacing: This is a poster-forward round. Use licensed poster artwork or studio-supplied assets; no audio is needed.

questions.prompt: Match each hit song to the film where it became a hit.

clips.label: (I’ve Had) The Time of My Life

questions.hostReveal: Dirty Dancing → (I’ve Had) The Time of My Life; Batman Forever → Kiss from a Rose; The Breakfast Club → Don’t You (Forget About Me); Saturday Night Fever → Stayin’ Alive; Top Gun → Take My Breath Away.

questions.prompt: Four of these films featured a song that won the Oscar for Best Original Song. Which one did not?
questions.imageAssetGuidance: Use licensed movie-poster images, displayed at equal size with accurate alt text.
questions.hostReveal: New York, New York is the surprise snub: its theme song was not nominated. Theme from Shaft, Skyfall, Beauty and the Beast, and Fame all won Best Original Song.

questions.prompt: For each actor and film, sort it into SANG IT or DIDN’T SING IT.

items.label: Christopher Plummer — The Sound of Music
Lady Gaga & Bradley Cooper — A Star Is Born

questions.hostReveal: SANG IT: Taron Egerton, Hugh Jackman, Joaquin Phoenix, Anne Hathaway, Lady Gaga & Bradley Cooper. DIDN’T SING IT: Rami Malek, Audrey Hepburn, Zac Efron, Christopher Plummer, Jamie Foxx.
questions.hostRevealNotes: Egerton performed every vocal in Rocketman. Phoenix and Witherspoon sang live in Walk the Line. Hathaway and the A Star Is Born leads recorded live on set. Malek’s vocals were a blend led by Freddie Mercury and Marc Martel; Hepburn was dubbed by Marni Nixon; Efron’s first High School Musical vocals were largely Drew Seeley; Plummer was dubbed by Bill Lee; Foxx lip-synced to Ray Charles while playing piano himself.

rounds.title: Round 3 — India’s Biggest Hits
rounds.intro: A welcoming, globally connected introduction to Indian music—built for people who may be hearing these stories for the first time.
rounds.hostPacing: Read each question clearly and use the reveals to add context rather than assuming prior knowledge.

questions.prompt: The song ‘Jai Ho’ won the Academy Award for Best Original Song in 2009. Which film was it from?
questions.hostReveal: Slumdog Millionaire. Composer A. R. Rahman won Oscars that night for both Original Song and Original Score.

questions.prompt: In 2023, ‘Naatu Naatu’ made history as the first song from an Indian production to win Best Original Song at the Oscars. Which film featured it?
questions.hostReveal: RRR. It’s a Telugu-language film—not Bollywood—and its global awards run was especially meaningful in South India.

questions.prompt: This 2003 global club hit paired British-Indian producer Panjabi MC with Jay-Z. Its instantly recognizable bassline is based on the theme song of which 1980s American TV show?
questions.hostReveal: Knight Rider. The original Mundian To Bach Ke was a Punjabi bhangra track; the Jay-Z version was released as Beware of the Boys.

questions.prompt: Sitar legend Ravi Shankar played both Woodstock and the Monterey Pop Festival. His daughter’s 2002 debut album won five Grammys and sold more than 20 million copies. Who is she?
questions.hostReveal: Norah Jones. Her half-sister, Anoushka Shankar, is also a Grammy-nominated sitarist.

questions.prompt: In 2023, this Punjabi singer and actor became the first Punjabi-language artist to perform at Coachella, taking the stage in a turban and kurta. Who is he?
questions.hostReveal: Diljit Dosanjh. He later brought Punjabi music to The Tonight Show and completed a major 2024 tour.

rounds.title: Round 4 — Finish the Lyric
rounds.intro: Tiny, familiar fragments only. Type the missing word or short phrase.
rounds.hostPacing: Keep each prompt visible for 15–20 seconds. Read it aloud once, but never sing or display a full lyric line.

questions.copyrightNote: Short fragment: four displayed lyric words plus one blank.

questions.prompt: Britney Spears: ‘Oh baby, baby, how was I supposed to ___.’
Rihanna: ‘We found love in a ___ place.’
The Killers: ‘I’ve got soul, but I’m not a ___.’
questions.hostReveal: Soldier — from All These Things That I’ve Done.

rounds.title: Round 5 — Piano Intro Finale
rounds.intro: Ten piano intros, ten titles, one full-board submission. Match every clip before time is up.
rounds.hostPacing: Play each clip in numerical order once (about 5–7 seconds each), then allow a 90-second open matching window. Replay individual clips on request. Lock all answers together; reveal one pair at a time.

questions.prompt: Match each numbered piano intro to its song title.
questions.hostReveal: Reveal in clip order: 1 Pink Pony Club; 2 Clocks; 3 Don’t Look Back in Anger; 4 Linus and Lucy; 5 I Will Survive; 6 Piano Man; 7 A Thousand Miles; 8 Let It Be; 9 Someone Like You; 10 Don’t Stop Believin’.
questions.assetProductionNote: Prefer cleared original recordings or newly commissioned/licensed piano performances. Ensure every clip begins cleanly, is loudness-normalized, and has a 100–200 ms fade in/out. Opaque asset IDs prevent accidental title leakage.

optionalTieBreak.prompt: Without looking it up: in what year was the first commercial compact disc released? Closest answer wins; over/under does not matter.
optionalTieBreak.hostReveal: 1982. Use only to break a tie after all 30 base points are scored.
optionalTieBreak.hostNote: Accept 1982; do not score it as a standard round question.
